A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SPARKE research. Their complete main texts and Appendices A–D are readable, and corresponding equations, tables, figures, and relocated material support reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix D report original Gaussian-mixture simulations, image-generation comparisons, kernel and guidance-scale analyses, and ControlNet examples.

after.justification: Original simulation and image-generation results remain, supplemented by reference-based novelty results and new quantitative model and computational-efficiency comparisons.

M1.justification: V2 presents a limited reference-image adaptation for novelty guidance (Section 5, Figure 6), while retaining the core conditional-RKE sampler. Algorithm 1 also changes the stated loss normalization from n^-4 to n^-2 times the squared Frobenius norm of the kernel product. Proposition 2 and Appendix B.2 retain the old normalization, so an implemented rescaling cannot be established.

E1.justification: The principal Gaussian-mixture, MS-COCO, and modified GeoDE coverage remains. V2 adds a reference-based novelty scenario involving cats and dogs, but removes the ControlNet pose-to-image example from v1 Appendix D/Figure 20. SDXL and PixArt were already evaluated in v1; their new quantitative table does not itself expand task coverage.

E2.justification: The main diversity-comparison methods remain unchanged. V2 Table 3 explicitly compares Pixel and DINOv2 variants of Particle Guide in the new efficiency experiment. Particle Guidance was already discussed as evaluated on Gaussian mixtures in v1, although its plotted and numerical results appear only in v2 Figure 4.

E3.justification: V2 introduces runtime and peak-memory evaluation over 1,000 generations with 50 diffusion steps on an RTX 4090, plus reference-category proportions for novelty evaluation. The SD2.1 comparison drops AuthPct, although SD1.5 retains it. Existing splits, sampling settings, and hyperparameter configurations in Appendix C remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds a case study testing suppression of reference categories and an empirical computational-cost analysis. The ControlNet case study is removed. Existing kernel-choice, diversity-guidance-strength, CFG-scale, and latent-versus-ambient analyses are retained, including their appendix evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the fixed-seed SD2.1 setup, SD1.5 seeds 0–4, and plus/minus reporting for Gaussian-mixture results. V2's new efficiency table also uses plus/minus values, but introduces no specified new uncertainty-estimation procedure, repeated-run scheme, or significance test.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantial results: SDXL/PixArt metrics in Table 2, efficiency measurements in Table 3, and novelty outcomes in Figure 6, where cats/dogs comprise 63% without guidance versus 15% with guidance. Particle Guide gains numerical Gaussian-mixture results. SD2.1 AuthPct values and ControlNet outcomes are removed. Retained SD1.5/SD2.1 scores and existing ablation curves are unchanged.

T1.justification: New Appendix B.3 introduces an interacting-particle stochastic differential equation, Equation 47, for SPARKE dynamics. Propositions 1–2 and their proofs remain essentially unchanged. Most other mathematical edits simplify formulas under explicit kernel normalization rather than establish new theoretical results.

C1.justification: V2 broadens the advertised contribution to novelty guidance in its title and explicitly claims guidance relative to reference data in Sections 2 and 5. The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion otherwise retain the original prompt-aware diversity and computational-scalability claims.

C2.justification: Appendix B.3 adds an interacting-particle and gradient-flow interpretation. Section 5 interprets the novelty example as avoiding reference categories and balancing other animals. The pose-conditioning applicability discussion is removed. The image-only limitation and proposed future modalities remain unchanged despite the expanded conclusion heading.

D1.justification: V2 documents the new efficiency benchmark's generation count, diffusion steps, and hardware, but removes v1's explicit general statement that evaluation scores use DINOv2 embeddings. Appendix C's existing implementation settings and the code-access link remain unchanged. The new novelty experiment provides little detail about reference-set construction or guidance configuration.

R1.justification: Section 2 expands positioning around novelty, finite-sample Vendi analysis, online/distributed model selection, and embedding alignment, adding corresponding references. It drops Rarity Score and several evaluation-metric references. The principal positioning against c-VSG, CADS, and Particle Guidance remains intact; publication and title updates to retained works are not new contributions.

P1.justification: V2 condenses related-work and experimental prose, relocates some latent-versus-ambient discussion to Appendix D, revises headings and author formatting, and adds acknowledgments. The abstract, introductory argument, main section sequence, and most proof and implementation prose remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: V2 substantially reorganizes the visual presentation through conference formatting, a new latent-versus-ambient workflow diagram, a novelty figure, and two new tables. It expands the Gaussian-mixture panel, restructures the SD2.1 table, relocates the ambient/latent table to Appendix D, and removes the ControlNet figure. Most existing image grids and ablation plots are reused and resized.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens empirical support through direct runtime/memory comparisons and quantitative SDXL/PixArt results that v1 lacked. These provide a modest overall gain despite removal of pose-conditioning and SD2.1 authenticity evidence. Sparse novelty-experiment documentation and the new normalization inconsistency between Algorithm 1 and Proposition 2 limit the improvement.
